title: Fine competitiveness of the discrete multiscale conditional-entropy metrical-task algorithm
author: Christian Coester and James R. Lee
work: Pure Entropic Regularization for Metrical Task Systems
source_version: Theory of Computing18 (2022), Article23, publisher source publicationDecember 29, 2022; DOI10.4086/toc.2022.v018a023

source_locator.proof_scope: Complete author argument including supplied core constructions

difficulty_reason: The selected algorithm must charge its positive movement to service cost despite the tree-dependent noise terms in the multiscale conditional-entropy regularizer. Section2 constructs local Bregman projections, a global service-cost divergence and a hybrid potential that controls noise-dominated motion before proving the finite competitiveness bounds, which are original obligations beyond a direct use of standard mirror descent.

source_check.note: Selected Theorem2.7: tau≥4 and the stated depth-dependent fine-competitiveness bounds for the authors’ discrete split-cost algorithm. Full Sections1–3 retained: Q_T/Delta and HST/weight assumptions, exact local projection algorithm, full service-cost and Lipschitz proofs, and complete movement/hybrid-potential core through1172. The HST-depth balancing fact and refined/global metric consequences remain support, not extra units. Original root-symbol tokens preserved with root-approved r-only installed-font renderer.
